title: Task-scoped escalations and human-only decision recording
context: Session start was asking about all pending escalations upfront, and agents were recording routine choices. This created unnecessary prompt noise and unclear ownership of what gets recorded. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Move escalation questions out of SessionStart and into the prompt hook, asking only about escalations touching the current task. Shift decision recording from agents to humans and commit synthesis; agents no longer record routine choices.
consequences: Escalations stay pending longer, asked only when a prompt touches related code
Significantly reduces prompt overhead at session start and during typical work
Clear human accountability for what gets recorded as a decision
Task-scoped context means fewer irrelevant escalations interrupt the flow
Requires hunch_escalations to surface pending items for explicit visibility
alternatives_rejected: Keep asking all escalations at SessionStart (bloats initial prompt with unrelated context)
Let agents continue recording routine choices (unclear ownership, unnecessary noise in memory)
Drop escalations entirely (loses important architectural context)

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Keep asking all escalations at SessionStart (bloats initial prompt with unrelated context)
Let agents continue recording routine choices (unclear ownership, unnecessary noise in memory)
